segments.text:
Builds the table `Table view of Figure 2: every interval` of the page. The page shows it folded: it stays closed until the reader opens it. It goes through the two panels (`P_OLD_BLOCKS` for the old read kernel, `P_NEW_BLOCKS` for the load-only loop). In each panel it goes through the blocks, the groups and the rows.
- Each group gets one title row: the panel name, the block title and the group title. The sub-title of the group (`g["sub"]`) follows when the group has one.
- Each row of the figure gets one table row with three cells: the label of the row with its notes, the number of intervals (`rg.n`), and the rate of every interval of the row (`rg.v`).
- These rates are the values of `val` for the records of the row. They are sorted from lowest to highest. `f2` rounds each one to 0.01 GB/s.
- No rate is summed or averaged here.
segments.heading: Function `detail_fig2`: table view of figure 2

segments.text: Finds in `FMD` (the text of FACTS.md) the part between `<summary>Words used here</summary>` and the next `</details>`. The script stops when this part is missing. Each line of the form `- **term**: definition` becomes one entry of the returned dictionary, from the term to its definition. Line 2290 stores the dictionary in `FW_WORDS`.
segments.heading: Function `facts_words`: the word list of FACTS.md

segments.text:
Returns the definition of the term `key` from `FW_WORDS` as HTML text. The script stops when the term is missing.
- `swap = (old, new)`: the phrase `old` is replaced by `new`. The script stops when `old` is not in the definition.
- Marks of the form `[RefN]`, with a number in place of N, are removed. `this sheet` becomes `this page`.
- `esc` escapes the HTML special characters. The double quotes are then written back as plain characters.
- A name between two backtick characters (the code marks of Markdown) becomes a `code` element.
- The first letter becomes a capital letter.
segments.heading: Function `fw`: one definition, copied for the page

segments.text:
These lines count the processes of part A. They read no rate. With the facts.json of this task they give 6 kernels, 24 processes per session and 4 used processes per session.
- `BOOT8`: the first 8 characters of the boot id of the rerun.
- `A_ALL`: all records of the dataset `rerun-A`, with every kernel and both binaries. `A_KERNELS`: those of six kernel names that occur in `A_ALL`.
- `A_PER_SESSION`: the number of processes of each session (different values of `proc_key`), as a sorted list of the different counts. `A_USED_PER_SESSION`: the same for the read processes that the page uses (`A_OLD + A_NEW`).
- `a_order`: for session 1 and each round, the pairs (binary, kernel) in the order of their launch time. Line 2314 stops unless round 1 has 12 such pairs and round 2 has the same 12 in the reverse order.
- Lines 2315 and 2316 stop unless part A holds only these kernels, the binaries `bw_old` and `bw_new`, and the rounds 1 and 2. The number of processes of every session must be the number of kernels x 2 x 2 (2 binaries, 2 rounds). With this data: 6 x 2 x 2 = 24. The number of used processes must be equal in all sessions.
segments.heading: Part A: process counts for the word list

segments.text:
- `LINE_TAGS`: the sorted tags of the records that the page uses from the rows L-1 to L-4 and from F72d12.
- Lines 2319 and 2320 stop unless these tags are `LINE_L`, `p1nop`, `p2add`, `thp`, `st1`, `st2` and `st3`. `LINE_L` (line 1196) is the name of the argument line in `like.spec`. It is `a6456` in that file.
- The same test also stops unless the csv file of each of these records of the rows L-1 to L-4 has the name of its tag plus `.csv`.
- `A3_TAGS`: the tags of row A-3. Line 2322 stops unless they are `onebuf-ms500-1` to `onebuf-ms500-3`.

`WORDS` is a list of pairs (term, definition). `build` (line 2677) writes it into the folded part `Words used here` of the page. These lines hold the first two entries.
- The entry `Q1, Q2` is typed. Typed means fixed text in the source, not a computed value.
- The entry `Rerun` takes four values from the data. The next three bullets name them.
- `GO_DONE` (line 874): the number of `done` lines in the log of go.sh. Line 875 asserts that it is 10.
- The start time and the end time of go.sh from `RERUN`. The slice `[11:19]` takes the time of day `HH:MM:SS` from the time stamp.
- `len(X_SEQ)` (line 1279): the number of kernels in the sequence of the older runner bwx. Line 1280 asserts that it is 8.
segments.heading: List `WORDS`: the word list of the page

segments.text:
Entries for the machine and for the kernels.
- A call of `fw` copies the definition from FACTS.md.
- The entries `Whole chip, 120 threads`, `Memory module` and `GB/s` are typed here.
- The entry `GB/s` states the unit of every rate of the page: 1 GB is 1e9 bytes.
- For `bwx12, bwx11, bwx` the `swap` argument replaces one sentence of the FACTS.md text by a longer one.

Entries for the method. These matter for the rates:
- `Rate` (line 2346) is copied from the FACTS.md entry `Rate, total`. It says how the page gets a rate. Part A: the column `aggregate_GBps` that bandwidth.c prints. bwx12 and bwx: the sum over the threads of bytes / elapsed time. The unit is GB/s.
- `Interval row, thread rows` (lines 2347 and 2348) says that the 120 thread rows of an interval follow its interval row.
- `Part A` (lines 2355 and 2356) prints the counts of lines 2309 to 2311: the processes per session, the kernel names, and the read processes that the page uses. It prints the difference as the number of the other processes, which the facts sheet holds. With this data: 24, 4 and 20 processes.
- Line 2345 prints `A_PER_SESSION[0] // 2`: the number of processes of one round (12 with this data).

Entries for the parts and for the earlier rows. The first two bullets name values from the data. The last two bullets name entries that say which intervals the page uses.
- `F72d12`: the launch time of the first record of `F_OLD`. `hm` (line 377) writes it as `HH:MM UTC`.
- The entry of lines 2364 and 2365 has the tags of `LINE_TAGS` as its term. The entry of line 2366 names the first and the last tag of row A-3.
- The entry `L-1, L-2, L-3, L-4` (line 2363) states which intervals the page takes from these rows: only `oldread` at position 0 and `asmread` at position 1. Lines 291 and 292 make this selection.
- The entry `Part L` (line 2357) says that the page does not use the three other test loops of a part L process. Lines 275 and 276 select only `oldread` at position 0 and `asmread` at position 1 from part L.

The other entries. Most are copied with `fw`, some with a changed phrase. The first three bullets name entries that state how the page compares rates. The last bullet names the one entry of these lines with a value from the data.
- `Pair, drop` (line 2372): the drop of a pair is (1 - load-only rate / old-kernel rate) x 100, in percent. In part A it uses the medians of the two processes of one session and round. This is the computation of `drop` (line 417) and of `a_pair` (line 444).
- `Pool`, `Overlap of two ranges` and `Distance of the nearest ends, farthest ends` give the terms of the comparison with the 8000 MT/s rows.
- `List of 8000 MT/s rows` (lines 2373 to 2375) names what the page leaves out. The bwx11 rows are not used. The rates of the bwx rows, of row X2d12 and of the three boots with 10 modules appear in notes under Table 2 only. Tables 5 and 6 name these rows and print no rate of them.
- `Boot, boot id` (line 2381) prints `BOOT8`.
Wraps a text in a `span` element of the class `num`. The style block (line 2638) keeps such a text on one line.
segments.heading: Function `nw`: a number that stays on one line

segments.text:
- `OLD_PARTS`: three pairs of ranges for the old read kernel. Each pair is a 7200 MT/s range and its 8000 MT/s range: part A with the pool A-1 to A-3, part C with the pool L-1 to L-4, part L with the same pool.
- Line 2405 stops unless the three overlap results are true, true, false. Sentence 2 of the Short version states this result.
- `c_ao`, `c_aa`: the drops of part C in percent, computed in lines 431 to 439. `c_ao` holds the drops of the 4 pairs with `read` directly after `oldread`. `c_aa` holds the drops of the 4 pairs with `read` directly after `asmread`.
- Line 2407 stops unless every record of `C_READ_AA` has `asmread` as its `kernel_before`.
- Line 2408 stops unless `VISIT_LO` is the lowest asmread rate of F72d12 and `VISIT_HI` is the highest asmread rate of part L.
- Line 2409 stops unless both orders have the same number of pairs. `c_all` joins the two lists: 8 drops.
segments.heading: Short version: tests before the three sentences

segments.text:
The three sentences hold percent values and counts. They hold no rate in GB/s.
- **Sentence 1** prints `min(c_all)` and `max(c_all)`: the lowest and the highest drop of the 8 pairs of part C. A pair is one interval of the bwx12 kernel `read` (the new read kernel) and the `oldread` interval of the same process and round. Its drop is (1 - rate of `read` / rate of `oldread`) x 100.
- Both rates are values of `val`: the sum of bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9 over the 120 thread rows of the interval (line 186), kept with 6 decimals. `f1` rounds a drop to 0.1 % only when it is printed.
- `len(c_all)` prints the number of pairs. The words `6 s measurements` are typed. Line 317 asserts a `min_ms` of 6000 (6 s) for these records.
- **Sentence 2** prints `L_OLD_NEAR_PCT` (line 491) and `L_OLD_MED_PCT` (line 492) for the old read kernel in part L. The first is the distance of the nearest ends in percent of the lower end of the 8000 MT/s range. The second is the difference of the medians in percent of the 8000 MT/s median.
- **Sentence 3** prints `len(RERUN_CMP_NEW)` (line 2066): the number of comparisons of the load-only loop of the rerun with 8000 MT/s rows. Line 2068 stops unless the 7200 MT/s range lies above the 8000 MT/s range in each of them.
- The saved output of a build shows 29.7 % to 31.2 % in 8 pairs, then 0.3 % and 1.3 %, then 4 comparisons [Ref5].
segments.heading: `SHORT`: the three sentences of the Short version

segments.text:
Three more tests of the sentences. Each one is a `need` call. The script stops when one of them fails.
- Line 2419: the text of n of part L must be equal for `oldread` and `asmread`. The same holds for the pool L-1 to L-4. Line 2426 prints one n for both kernels.
- Line 2421: sentence 3 must hold the phrase `in all N comparisons of the rerun (Table 2)`, with N from `RERUN_CMP_NEW`. Line 2416 types the same phrase. So this test can fail only after an edit of that line.
- Line 2422: the asmread range of F72d12 must lie inside the range of the 8000 MT/s pool. Its highest value must be below the lowest asmread value of part L.

`UL` (line 1493) returns an HTML bullet list and adds its items to `PROSE` for the word count. The five items print these computed values:
- Item 1: the lowest and the highest drop of `c_ao` and of `c_aa`, each with 1 decimal, and the number of pairs per order.
- Item 2, part L: n at 7200 MT/s and at 8000 MT/s. For the old read kernel it prints the two ranges (`rL_old`, `rPL_old`), the distance of the nearest ends `abs(L_OLD_NEAR)` and the difference of the medians `abs(L_OLD_MED)` in GB/s, and both in percent. For asmread it prints the two ranges (`rL_asm`, `rPL_asm`).
- Item 3: `width_pct` (line 476) of the two 8000 MT/s ranges of the old read kernel. It is the width of a range in percent of its lower end. The page marks it `est.`.
- Item 4: `len(RERUN_CMP_NEW) - RERUN_CMP_C`, the number of comparisons that stay without part C. `RERUN_CMP_C` is the constant 1 of line 2067.
- Item 5: the asmread range of F72d12, its n, and `abs(DIST['nearest'][1])`. This is the distance of the nearest ends between part L and F72d12 (line 504).
- A range text comes from `Rg.txt` (line 204): the lowest and the highest rate, each rounded to 0.01 GB/s by `f2`.
segments.heading: `SHORT_MORE`: five items under the Short version

segments.text:
- `l1d`: the drops of the 2 pairs of row L-1 (8000 MT/s).
- `GO_SECS`: the run time of go.sh in seconds. It is the end time of day minus the start time of day (`secs`, line 983).
- `N_RERUN_PAIRS`: the numbers of pairs of part C, part L and part A. For part A a pair is a pair of process medians. With this data: 8, 6 and 6 pairs.
- Line 2440 stops unless these numbers plus the pairs of control I and of F72d12 give the length of `ALL_7200_DROPS` (line 459).
- `C_ASM_DROPS`: part C times asmread too. `pairs_in_process` pairs each asmread interval of part C with the `oldread` interval of the same process and round. `drops_of` computes the drop of each pair.
- Line 2443 stops unless there are 8 such drops and each one is above 0. The page uses only their number, in the caption of Table 1 (line 2735).
segments.heading: Pair counts for section 1

segments.text:
`SEC1_INTRO` and `SEC1_AFTER` are the bullet lists before and after figure 1 and Table 1. Their computed values:
- The start time and the end time of go.sh, and `BOOT8`.
- `drop_txt` (line 425) of the drops of part L, of control I and of F72d12. It prints the lowest and the highest drop with 1 decimal. It prints one value when both print equal.
- `drop_txt(l1d)`: the same for row L-1 at 8000 MT/s. The page file on disk (`OUT`, line 31) shows 35.9 % to 36.1 % for it.
- The saved output of a build shows 29.2 % to 30.5 % for part L, 31.9 % to 32.8 % for control I and 35.4 % for F72d12 [Ref5].
segments.heading: Text of section 1 (question Q1)

segments.text:
- `SEC2_INTRO` states the comparison rule. The rule compares the lowest-to-highest range of the 7200 MT/s intervals with that of the 8000 MT/s rows.
- `SEC2_INTRO` then gives the fixed wording of each result. For an overlap it is `WORD_SAME` (line 470): `no difference seen`. For no overlap it is `WORD_DIFF` (line 471).
- Table 2 has two rows without an overlap that do not hold `WORD_DIFF`. They are the part A rows of the new read kernel. Line 2107 writes `outside (above) the 8000 MT/s range of the same round` there.
- `SEC2_BOOT` prints `VISIT_LO` and `VISIT_HI` (line 501): the lowest and the highest asmread rate of the three visits of the part L line in the 7200 MT/s boot. It also prints their difference.
- The saved output of a build shows 301.90 to 327.93 GB/s and a difference of 26.03 GB/s [Ref5].
segments.heading: Text of section 2 (question Q2)

segments.text: Six typed items for the page section `What the data do not show`. Each one names a point that the data do not show, and the measurement that would resolve it. No computed value is printed here.
segments.heading: `INSUFF`: text of section 3

segments.text:
- `go_first`: the entry of `meta.launches` for the first step, T72A1.
- `others`: the 1-minute load average at the first launch of the steps 2 to 10 of go.sh (`STEPS[1:10]`, T72L1 to T72C4).
- Line 2480 stops unless each of these 9 steps has a `gap_s` of 5. Table 6 prints this field as the time in seconds since the end of the previous 120-thread process (line 2252).
- Line 2481 stops unless T72A1 has no gap. Line 2482 stops unless its load average was below 1 (an idle start).
segments.heading: Load at launch: facts for Table 6 and for figure 2

segments.text:
Facts for the reading notes under figure 2 (the list `how2`, line 2684).
- Line 2486 stops unless part A of sessions 2 and 3 started 5 s after a part C process. The test reads `gap_s` and the text `start_state` of the two entries of `LAUNCH`.
- `A_FIRST_LOAD`: the 1-minute load average at the first launch of T72A1 and of the rows A-1 and A-2. For a row, `first` is the record with the earliest launch time of the whole dataset.
- Line 2490 stops unless `first` is a `bw_old` read record that the page uses, from the first process of its csv file, in round 1.
- Line 2492 stops unless the three load values are below 2.
- `a_sess_n`: for each session of `A_OLD`, the number of intervals and the number of processes. Line 2494 stops unless every session has 6 intervals of 2 processes. `A_SESSION_N` is the typed text of this n.
Returns an HTML list of the class `cl` with one item per argument.
segments.heading: Function `cl`: bullet list inside a table cell

segments.text:
Builds Table 5 of the page section `Machine state and system load`. Each row has three cells: a fact, its proof and its limit.
- `LOWEST_ASM` (line 520) is the record with the lowest asmread rate of the pool L-1 to L-4. `low_day` is the date of its launch.
- Line 2506 stops unless the first hardware error record of that interval (`HW_LOW`, line 1031) has the same date, and the date is 2026-11-15.
segments.heading: Function `state_table`: Table 5, the machine state

segments.text:
Rows 1 to 6 of the table. They hold no rate. Their values come from `RERUN` (the entry `meta.rerun` of facts.json) and from the raw-file checks of lines 811 to 1386. Lines 865, 866, 877 and 878 stop unless the run logs hold the same boot id, the same `MemTotal` and the same times as `RERUN`.
- 12 memory modules: `MemTotal` of all state lines, the record of the boot in try6.txt (`TRY6_UTC`, `TRY6_MODLINE`) and the counts of the module list (`DMI_N`, `DMI_SIZE`).
- Memory speed 7200 MT/s: the boot id and the record of the boot. The limit cell says that the speed was not read during the rerun.
- The rerun is complete: the times of go.sh and `GO_DONE`, the number of `done` lines of its log.
- Logins and accounts: the number of state lines of the go.sh log and the accounts that own processes.
- Control I: the times of go2.sh.
- F72d12: the boot list (`BOOT_FIRST`, `BOOT_LAST`) and the times of the F72d12 process (`F_LAUNCH`, `F_END`).

Rows 7 to 9.
- Work before the first 120-thread process: the number and the times of the one-thread processes of 2026-11-13. This row prints one range of rates: `rA12_old.txt()`. It is the lowest and the highest rate of `bw_old` read over the 12 intervals of the rows A-1 and A-2 (line 1362). The saved output of a build shows 464.42 to 467.06 GB/s [Ref5].
- Firmware settings: the times of the changes of the two TXREQ settings, the number of entries of the settings list (`N_SET`), the entries without a readable value (`N_UNREAD`), and the file time of the change to 7200 MT/s (`D72_T`).
- The 8000 MT/s rows: the start and the end of the saved kernel log of that boot. The row also prints `MEM_LESS_GIB` (line 1157): how many GiB less memory the kernel log of one boot with 10 modules shows than the kernel log of the 8000 MT/s boot (1 GiB is 2^30 bytes).

Rows 10 and 11, and the return.
- Row 10 prints the numbers of corrected hardware error records in the journal during the rows L-1 to L-4 (`HW_L1`, `HW_L2`, `HW_L34`) and during the rows A-1 to A-3 (`HW_A`).
- Row 11 prints `f2(val(LOWEST_ASM))`: the lowest asmread rate of the pool. It is the value of `val` for that one interval: the sum of bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9 over its 120 thread rows. `LOW_FROM` and `LOW_TO` (line 1030) are the start time and the end time of the interval: the launch time plus the seconds since the process start in the thread rows. The page marks them `est.`.
- Row 11 also prints the range of the pool without this one interval (`rPL_asm_wo`, line 521) and the asmread range of part L (`rL_asm`), each with its n. It prints `rL_asm.nearest(rPL_asm_wo)` too: the lowest asmread rate of part L minus the highest rate of that smaller pool.
- The saved output of a build shows 288.54 GB/s for the lowest value, 298.61 to 309.17 GB/s for the pool without it, and 321.65 to 327.93 GB/s for part L [Ref5].
- Line 2570 passes the rows to `table` (line 1501) with the column titles `Fact`, `Proof` and `Limit`.

Prints the 1-minute load average at the first launch of the rerun (`go_first`). Then it prints the lowest and the highest load of `others`, the 9 other steps of go.sh. The text states a hypothesis that was not tested: the high values come from the 120-thread processes of the rerun itself. In `meta.launches` of facts.json the first launch has a load average of 0.07, and the other 9 steps have 74.05 to 105.24 [Ref2].
segments.heading: `LOAD_CAPTION`: caption text of Table 6

segments.text:
A text constant with the style rules of the page. `build` puts it into the `style` element (line 2707). It holds no data. This first part sets:
- one light colour theme (`color-scheme:light`) and a page width of at most 980 px (pixels).
- the headings, the box of the Short version and the word list in two columns (one column in a window of at most 600 px).
- the base style of the tables. A cell of the class `n` is right-aligned.
segments.heading: `CSS`: the style block of the page

segments.text:
Width rules.
- The wide tables (classes `q1`, `q2`, `state`, `load`, `visits` and `detail`) have a least width of 900 px. In a window below 949 px such a table can scroll sideways.
- The rule of line 2615 shows a hint line in a window of at most 949 px. Line 2617 shows a second hint for the panels of figure 2 in a window of at most 519 px.
- Most of the other rules set the least width of single columns.
- The class `num` (line 2638) keeps a number and its unit on one line.

Rules for the figures and for the rest of the page.
- Figure 1 exists in three layouts (classes `f1w`, `f1m` and `f1n`). The rules show the wide one in a window of 1000 px or more, the middle one from 780 px to 999 px, and the narrow one below 780 px.
- The two panels of figure 2 stand side by side when the window is wide enough.
- The other rules style more parts of the page. Among them are the legends, a dot under the pointer, the captions, the reference marks, the reference list and the folded parts.

`words`: one pair of the HTML elements `dt` (term) and `dd` (definition) per entry of `WORDS`. `short`: one paragraph per sentence of `SHORT`. `P` (line 1488) also adds each sentence to `PROSE` for the word count.
segments.heading: Function `build`: the whole page as one text

segments.text:
`how1` and `how2` are the reading notes under figure 1 and under figure 2.
- `how1` says that each dot of figure 1 is the median of the intervals of its row. `fig1` places the dots at these medians (line 1662).
- `how1` then tells the reader how a bwx12 rate is computed. The source text of a tooltip (`src`, line 359) names the interval row of the csv file. The rate is the sum over the 120 thread rows after it: `val` (line 176) adds bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9 of each thread row.
- It prints `f2(IROW_MAX)` (line 342). `IROW_MAX` is the largest difference between this sum, rounded to 0.01 GB/s, and the rate printed in the interval row, over the bwx12 records of `USED`. Line 343 allows at most 0.02 GB/s. The saved output of a build shows 0.02 GB/s [Ref5].
- `how2` says that a 7200 MT/s row without bold text is not compared with the grey band of its block (the range of the 8000 MT/s rows). In the 0.5 s blocks of the panel `Load-only loop` (part A, `bw_new` read) only session 1 is compared, each round against the same round. `A_V3` (line 509) holds these two comparisons.
- `how2` prints the three load values of `A_FIRST_LOAD`, the number of dots `N_DOTS` (line 1960) and the text `A_SESSION_N`.

`fig2` holds the two panels of figure 2. `panel` (line 1756) draws each one.
- Panel `Old read kernel`: the blocks `P_OLD_BLOCKS`, blue dots, an x axis from 458 to 476 GB/s (`OLD_AX`).
- Panel `Load-only loop`: the blocks `P_NEW_BLOCKS`, orange dots, an x axis from 276 to 340 GB/s (`NEW_AX`).
- The two `range` arguments of a call give the grid lines. The first panel has a grid line every 2 GB/s and a label every 4 GB/s. The second panel has a grid line every 10 GB/s and a label every 20 GB/s.
- Neither axis starts at 0. `panel` writes this into each panel (lines 1793 and 1820).

The page text starts here. It is one f-string that ends in line 2780. These lines write:
- the head of the page with the style block and the title.
- a typed line with the machine and the method: 120 threads on CPUs 0-119, 256 MiB per thread, 12 memory modules at 7200 MT/s.
- the box with the three sentences (`short`) and the list `SHORT_MORE`.
- the folded word list (`words`).

Page section 1 (question Q1).
- `SEC1_INTRO`, the legend `LEG1`, and figure 1 three times: `fig1` (line 1593) with the layouts `wide`, `mid` and `narrow`.
- The caption of figure 1 prints `len(SAME_LINE_ROWS)`. Line 1588 asserts 6 rows. It prints two differences: `VISIT_OLD_HI - VISIT_OLD_LO` for the old read kernel and `VISIT_HI - VISIT_LO` for the load-only loop (lines 501 and 502). Each one is the highest minus the lowest interval rate over part L, control I and F72d12. The caption also prints these four rates as two ranges.
- The caption of Table 1 prints `sum(N_RERUN_PAIRS)` and `len(C_ASM_DROPS)`.
- `q1_table()` (line 2003) builds Table 1, the drop per part. `SEC1_AFTER` follows.
- `detail_fig1()` (line 2255) builds the folded table view of figure 1.

Page section 2 (question Q2).
- `SEC2_INTRO`, the legend `LEG2`, and a note on the scales. The first panel shows 18 GB/s over its width and the second shows 64 GB/s. The note prints the ratio with 1 decimal: 3.6.
- `fig2` and its caption. The caption prints `F2_RIGHT_TXT` (line 1954), `abs(L_OLD_NEAR)` and `abs(L_OLD_MED)`.
- The caption of Table 2 prints `GO_DONE`, the run time `GO_SECS` as minutes and seconds, and `T2_RERUN_ROWS` (line 2074). `q2_table()` (line 2079) builds Table 2.
- `SEC2_BOOT`, then Table 3 from `visits_table()` (line 2184).
- Table 4 from `dist_table()` (line 2213). Its caption prints the texts of n of part L, of the pool L-1 to L-4 and of F72d12.
- `detail_fig2()` (line 2266) builds the folded table view of figure 2.
Page sections 3 and 4. Section 3 is the list `INSUFF`. Section 4 holds Table 5 from `state_table()` (line 2503), and Table 6 from `load_table()` (line 2219) with the caption text `LOAD_CAPTION`.

The reference section of the page.
- A typed note says that a script computed every rate from the interval records of the facts sheet and from the thread rows of the csv files that these records name.
- Line 2775 prints the two folder paths `R` and `S`.
- `\x01REFLIST\x01` (the word REFLIST between two control characters) is a placeholder. `number_refs` replaces it by the reference list.
- Line 2781 returns the page text.

Line 2784 calls `build`. All figure functions and table functions run inside this call.
- `number_refs` (line 828) then replaces each reference mark by `[RefN]`, numbered in the order of first use, and writes the reference list.
- `PAGE` is the finished page text.
- `UNCITED` is the list of the reference keys that the page never cites.
segments.heading: Build the page and number the references

segments.text:
Each `check` call adds one PASS or FAIL line to `CHECKS`. The script does not stop here.
- `words_n`: the number of words in `PROSE`, the texts that `P` and `UL` collected. `strip_tags` (line 1484) removes the tags and the reference marks first. A word is a run of characters without white space that holds a letter or a digit. `how_n` is the same count for the reading notes under the two figures.
- Line 2789: `words_n` must be from 700 to 1000 words.
- Line 2791: `SHORT` must hold 3 texts, each with exactly one sentence end. A sentence end is `.`, `!` or `?` before white space or at the end of the text. A decimal point does not count. A full stop directly after `MT/s` does not count.
- Line 2792: no reference may be uncited.
- Line 2793: the page must hold none of the texts `prefers-color-scheme`, `<script`, `<link`, `@import`, `url(`, `<img` and `src=`. So it has one colour theme, no script and no external file.
segments.heading: Checks of the built page

segments.text:
- `units`: the texts of the `li`, `p`, `figcaption`, `title`, `dd` and `tr` elements of the page. A list item inside a table row is not a unit of its own. It belongs to the unit of that row.
- The loop runs once for control I and once for F72d12. `hit` holds the units that name it. `miss` holds those of them without its label. The label is `added after the first numbers were seen` for control I and `not part of the rerun` for F72d12.
- The check of line 2800 passes when `hit` is not empty and `miss` is empty.
- Line 2801 counts the `<title>` tags of the page and subtracts 1 for the page title. The rest are tooltips. The check passes when their number is at least `N_DOTS + 2 * F1_NROWS`.
- This is a lower limit: 139 + 2 x 21 = 181 tooltips with this data. The message prints `3 * F1_NROWS`, not the limit of the test. The saved output of a build shows 333 tooltips [Ref5].

- `VISIBLE`: the text of the page without the style block and without tags. It includes the tooltips.
- `BANNED`: 16 phrases that a review rejected. The semicolon is one of them. The check of line 2807 passes when none of them is in `VISIBLE`.
- `bare`: every place where `kernel thread`, `kernel line` or `kernel message` stands without `Linux` directly before it. The check of line 2811 passes when this list is empty.

The last check covers the hover areas of figure 2.
- `panel` adds one entry per panel to `F2_GAPS` (line 1788). The entry holds the title, the number of dots, the smallest distance of two dots in px, the number of hover areas that a neighbour cuts, and the size of every hover area.
- The check passes when there are 2 panels, and the number of dots and the number of areas both equal `N_DOTS`.
- Its message reports the smallest distance, the smallest area and the median area.

Prints one line per entry of `CHECKS`, with `PASS` or `FAIL` before its text.
- `bad` counts the FAIL lines. Line 2824 prints how many checks pass.
- When `bad` is above 0, the script prints `NOT WRITTEN` and ends with exit status 1 (`sys.exit(1)`).
- The output file is not opened in that case. So the page on disk stays as it was.
segments.heading: Print the self-check list and decide

segments.text:
The only write of the script. It runs only when every check passed and no `need` call stopped the script before.
- Lines 2828 to 2830 encode `PAGE` as UTF-8 (the usual byte encoding of text) and write the bytes to `OUT` (line 31). An older page file is replaced.
- Line 2831 prints the path, the size in bytes and the number of characters.
- Lines 2832 to 2834 print the three sentences of `SHORT` as plain text: without tags, and with each run of white space as one space.
- The saved output of a build shows 98 of 98 checks as PASS and a page of 425796 bytes [Ref5].
- Line 2834 is the last line of the file.
